A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same WebFactory study, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I. Pages 3–22 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; changes are confined to the first two pages.

before.justification: v1 reports original task-generation, trajectory-quality, and agent-evaluation experiments in Section 3, Tables 1–5, and Figure 3. Appendix F also reports analyses of the generated trajectory dataset.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and dataset analyses, including the offline benchmark, online-transfer evaluation, and public GUI benchmark results.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Appendices C–G retain the same environment synthesis, task generation, trajectory filtering, action space, reward functions, and GRPO training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten offline website families, operational and retrieval tasks, Amazon/Airbnb/Booking transfer scenarios, and public GUI benchmark coverage, including the ScreenSpot evaluations in Figure 3.

E2.justification: Tables 3–5 retain QwenVL2.5-3B, GPT-4o, and GUI-R1-3B in the same comparisons. The foundation-model comparisons in Section 3.4 and Figure 3 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings remain identical, including 100 offline tasks, 30 tasks per online platform, the reported metrics, Appendix I's task-construction and feasibility checks, and Appendix H's training settings.

E4.justification: The knowledge/data ablations in Tables 1–2, foundation-model analysis in Figure 3, and action-distribution and transition analyses in Appendix F are identical. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix I.3 retains the same 95% Wilson confidence intervals for the 90-task transfer evaluation. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 4 retains average transfer TCRs of 53.4% for WebFactory-3B and 37.0% for GUI-R1-3B; the results in Figures 3–5 also match.

T1.justification: The action-space and reward definitions in Section 2.2.3 and Appendix G, including Equations 1–4, are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The claims concerning synthetic-data efficiency, generalization, intelligence compression, and foundation-model embodiment potential are unchanged. The open-source toolchain contribution was already claimed in v1's introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations are unchanged. Section 4 still identifies the lack of exhaustive reward ablations and incomplete validation on fundamentally different GUI paradigms.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract adds a direct GitHub repository URL for WebFactory's code and resources. v1 already described an open-source release but supplied no project repository URL. Implementation details and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The references and Appendix B are identical, preserving the same positioning relative to offline benchmarks, live-web generation, and weak-supervision pipelines.

P1.justification: v2 appends one code-and-resources availability sentence to the abstract and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining wording and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded abstract changes line wrapping and pushes the final two lines of an introductory paragraph onto page 2, with corresponding spacing adjustments. All figures, tables, and layouts from page 3 onward are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies a prominent repository address where v1 only claimed an open-source release, modestly improving resource discoverability and reproducibility documentation. The scientific content and appendices are unchanged. The PDFs establish this documentation gain, but do not establish the linked repository's completeness or usability.
